arxiv-2202-12045.description: Abstract We investigate the reconfiguration of n n blocks, or “tokens”, in the square grid using line pushes . A line push is performed from one of the four cardinal directions and pushes all tokens that are maximum in that direction to the opposite direction by one unit.

arxiv-2206-03685.title: On pointwise error estimates for Voronoï-based finite volume methods for the Poisson equation on the sphere
arxiv-2206-03685.creator: Leonardo A. Poveda, Pedro Peixoto
arxiv-2206-03685.description: Abstract In this paper, we give pointwise estimates of a Voronoï-based finite volume approximation of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on Voronoï-Delaunay decompositions of the sphere. These estimates are the basis for a local error analysis, in the maximum norm, of the approximate solution of the Poisson equation and its gradient.

arxiv-2405-17696.title: Physics-guided Full Waveform Inversion using Encoder-Solver Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2405-17696.creator: Matan M. Goren, Eran Treister 0
arxiv-2405-17696.description: Abstract Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) is an inverse problem for estimating the wave velocity distribution in a given domain, based on observed data on the boundaries. The inversion is computationally demanding because we are required to solve multiple forward problems, either in time or frequency domains, to simulate data that are then iteratively fitted to the observed data.

arxiv-2409-18752.title: Royal Reveals: LiDAR Mapping of Kronborg Castle, Echoes of Hamlet’s Halls
arxiv-2409-18752.creator: Leon Davies, Simon Sølvsten
arxiv-2409-18752.description: Abstract This paper presents a large scale dataset from a meticulous 360-degree LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) scan conducted on Kronborg Castle, a renowned Renaissance fortress located in Elsinore (Helsingør), Denmark, famously associated with Shakespeare’s ”Hamlet.” Utilising a vertical mounted, gimbal stabilised, 16 channel, 360-degree Velodyne VLP-16 LiDAR scanner, paired with an Intel RealSense L515 depth camera.

arxiv-2505-00644.title: Predatory dynamics in susceptible and resistant Eriopis connexa populations Journal: Ecological Complexity
arxiv-2505-00644.creator: Anna Mara Ferreira Maciel, Gabriel Rodrigues Palma, Lucas dos Anjos, Lucas Santos Canuto, Wesley Augusto Conde Godoy, Rafael de Andrade Moral
arxiv-2505-00644.description: Abstract The ladybird Eriopis connexa (Germar, 1824), a voracious aphid predator, faces challenges from insecticide applications, compromising biological control. As a result, there has been an increase in the number of studies analysing the resistance and susceptibility of ladybirds. Some studies have found that resistant populations exhibit distinct predation and foraging behaviour compared to susceptible ones.

Using the convex structure of the space of q q -exchangeable probability measures, we show that the optimal rate of convergence is of order q n q^{n} . 1.

arxiv-2507-01076.title: Empirical Analysis Of Heuristic and Approximation Algorithms for the The Mutual-Visibility Problem DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Student Computing Research Symposium; September 10, 2025; Ljubljana, Slovenia Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
arxiv-2507-01076.creator: Vanja Stojanović, Bor Pangeršič
arxiv-2507-01076.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vanja Stojanović, Bor Pangeršič. The NP-complete mutual-visibility (MV) problem currently lacks empirical analysis on its practical behaviour despite theoretical studies. This paper addresses this gap by implementing and evaluating three distinct algorithms – a direct random heuristic, a hypergraph-based approximation, and a genetic algorithm – on diverse synthetic graph datasets, including those with analytically known μ ⁡ ( G ) \mu(G) values and general graph models. Our results demonstrate that for smaller graphs, the algorithms consistently achieve MV set sizes aligning with theoretical bounds.

arxiv-2507-22264.title: SmartCLIP: Modular Vision-language Alignment with Identification Guarantees
arxiv-2507-22264.creator: Shaoan Xie*, Lingjing Kong*, Yujia Zheng, Yu Yao, Zeyu Tang, Eric P. Xing, Guangyi Chen, Kun Zhang
arxiv-2507-22264.description: Abstract Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) ( Radford et al. 2021 ) has emerged as a pivotal model in computer vision and multimodal learning, achieving state-of-the-art performance at aligning visual and textual representations through contrastive learning. However, CLIP struggles with potential information misalignment in many image-text datasets and suffers from entangled representation.

arxiv-2511-19032.title: Benchmarking Corruption Robustness of LVLMs: A Discriminative Benchmark and Robustness Alignment Metric
arxiv-2511-19032.creator: Xiangjie Sui, Songyang Li, Hanwei Zhu, Baoliang Chen, Yuming Fang, Xin Sun
arxiv-2511-19032.description: Abstract Despite the remarkable reasoning abilities of large vision–language models (LVLMs), their robustness under visual corruptions remains insufficiently studied. Existing evaluation paradigms exhibit two major limitations: 1) the dominance of low-discriminative samples in current datasets masks the real robustness gap between models; and 2) conventional accuracy-based metric fail to capture the degradation of the underlying prediction structure.

pmc-10603108.description: OAuth2.0 is a Single Sign-On approach that helps to authorize users to log into multiple applications without re-entering the credentials. pmc-11327247.description: Numerous observational studies have suggested a potential causal relationship between skipping breakfast and cardiovascular diseases, including heart failure (HF). However, these studies are susceptible to inherent confounders and the challenge of reverse causation, and the underlying metabolic factors are not yet clear.

pmc-11459997.title: Burnout amongst chiropractic faculty, practitioners, and trainees: a scoping review

pmc-13070330.title: Retrospective Analysis of Infection Characteristics and Prognostic Factors in ICU Sepsis Patients in Jiaxing Area
pmc-13070330.creator: Hui Li, Xiaochun Tan, Siheng Wang, Weifeng Shen, Beibei Yuan
pmc-13070330.description: BackgroundSepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in intensive care units (ICUs), with antimicrobial resistance (AMR) complicating therapeutic decisions. Clinical outcomes, pathogen profiles, and antimicrobial susceptibility were evaluated.

pmc-13146105.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A839 VIDEO STREAMING DURING EMERGENCY CALLS: EFFECT ON STROKE RECOGNITION AND PREHOSPITAL CARE—A PREDEFINED SUBSTUDY OF THE CAM-VISION TRIAL
pmc-13146105.creator: Rolf Blauenfeldt, Ulla Væggemose, Claus Ziegler Simonsen, Martin Faurholdt Gude
pmc-13146105.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and aimsEarly recognition of stroke during emergency calls is crucial for timely reperfusion treatment, but dispatcher diagnostic accuracy varies widely. Whether live video streaming between callers and dispatchers improves stroke recognition and care is unclear. This is a predefined substudy of the cluster-randomized CAM-VISION trial evaluated the effect of dispatcher access to live video on identification of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) and prehospital management.MethodsDispatchers were randomized to use either live one-way video from callers’ smartphones or standard telephone communication.

pmc-13227501.description: This study investigated the photocatalytic degradation of methylene blue (MB) using four commercial TiO2 photocatalysts (P25, P90, PC105, PC500) in suspension under 365 nm UV-LED irradiation, with the reaction monitored by UV–Vis spectrometry. Among these, P25 showed the highest activity and was subsequently immobilised on metal plates.

pmc-13262919.title: Effect of Saurauia vulcani leaf extract on spleen morphometric and histopathological changes in rats infected with Salmonella typhimurium

This study aimed to evaluate the effect of S. vulcani leaf extract on spleen morphometry and histopathology in rats infected with Salmonella typhimurium.

pmc-13325733.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Although prior studies have demonstrated efficacy and general tolerability, a comprehensive evaluation of its safety profile across later-stage clinical trials is needed.MethodsSafety outcomes were assessed in a pooled analysis of two phase III trials comparing obicetrapib 10 mg daily with placebo in adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Participants received treatment for 365 days.

pmc-13594186.creator: Carla Kirschbaum, Sophie A S Lawrence, Jack L Bennett, Olivia B Ramsay, Yara Ahmed, Tarick J El-Baba, Stefano Vanni, Carol V Robinson
